Brushware Sectional Committee, CHD 24

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Brushware Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Hair brushes constitute an item for household use. It is also required by the defence services in sufficient quantity. There is no ISO standard on this subject. This standard has been prepared based on indigenous manufacturers' data. This standard was originally published in 1968 based on the Defence Specification lND/GS/927(a): 1960 'Brushes, hair' issued by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India . In the light of experiences gained in last 30 years, the Committee felt a need to revise this standard to meet the present requirement based on the technological advancement in this area. In this revision, weight of filling material has been reduced as it does not affect the performance, shelf-life has been introduced and tolerances on the linear dimensions have been increased. The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex D. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard BRUSHES, HAIR -- SPECIFICATION ( First Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes requirements, methods of sampling and test for hair brushes manufactured from black nylon monofilament or black bristles. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 380 : 1978 384 : 1979 1843 : 1963 1844 : 1993 3451(Part2): 1975 Title French chalk, technical (second revision) Brushes, paints and varnishes, flat (fourth revision) Nylon monofilaments Bristles (second revision) Code of practice for care and maintenance of brushes: Part 2 Brushes other than pan set brushes 5.1.2 Handle The handle shall be made of timber or plastics. 5.1.2.1 The plastic handle shall be made from high density thermosetting or thermoplastic resin. 5.1.2.2 Any of the timber species listed in Annex A shall be used in the manufacture of the wooden portion of the brush. 5.1.2.3 The timber shall be reasonably straight-grained and well-seasoned to a moisture content not exceeding 15 percent, when tested either by any electronic moisture meter or by the oven dry method given in Annex B. In case of dispute, the oven dry method shall be used. 5.1.2.4 The timber shall be free from brashness, any kind of decay (rot), insect attack, centre heart (pith) knots (except pin knots) crack, wrap and any other defect which may reduce the life of the brush or effect its utility. 5.1.3 Wire Galvanized wire of 0.38 � 0.05 mm diameter shall be used 5.1.4 Staples Staples of bright iron wire or copper coated mild steel wire of 0.60 � 0.05 mm diameter shall be used. 5.1.5 Nails for Wooden Handle Steel/Iron nails, 10 � 1 mm long and 1.00 to 1.30 mm in diameter shall be used for securing back cover the exposed portion of the board. 5.2 Manufacture 5.2.1 The shape and design of the brushes shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 5.2.2 The back and board if made of timber, shall be manufactured from one piece of timber. 5.2.3 The back shall be re-inforced securely glued to the board and reinforced with 8 steel nails as shown in Fig. 1 in such a manner that they do not foul the wire or the filling material. 5.2.4 The board shall be drilled with 242 tuft holes of the shape and size as indicated in Fig. 1. 5.2.5 For Wire Draft Brushes The tufts of filling material shall be firmly drawn into

not apply to filling material for which minimum lengths have been prescribed (see Fig. 1). 5.4 Weight of Filling Material The total weight of the filling material per brush, when determined after unfastening the tufts by removal of galvanized wire or staples, using a suitable weighing balance, shall be 15 g for Type 1 and 18 g for Type 2. A tolerance of �5 percent shall be allowed on the weight of filling material. 3

5.5 Knock Back Test The knots shall not enter into the tufts holes and the working surface shall not be uneven when the brush is knocked at the back. 5.6 Shelf-Life The brushes shall have a shelf-life of one year from the date of manufacture provided proper storage conditions are used and adequate precautions are taken for preserving them as given in 4 of IS 3451 (Part 2).

IS 4584 : 2002 5.7 Workmanship and Finish 5.7.1 The handle of the brush shall be smoothly finished and suitably waxed, polished or lacquered. 5.7.2 In general workmanship and finish, the brush shall match the approved sample. 5.7.3 At least 70 percent of the bristle shall be free from flag ends. 5.8 Preservation The filling material of the brush shall be liberally dusted with a mixture of 5 parts (by mass) of DDT dusting powder and 95 percent by mass of french chalk ( see IS 380). 6 PACKING AND MARKING 6.1 Packing The hair brushes shall be wrapped with cellulose paper so as to ensure retention of the preservative and shall further be packed in card board boxes or as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.2 Marking 6.2.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the indentor or inspection authority and the supplier, each brush shall be legibly and indelibly marked or stamped with the manufacturer's name or recognized trade-mark, if any, and the year of manufacture. 6.3 BIS Certification Marking The brushes may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 6.3.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 7 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY The method of drawing representative samples of the material and the criteria of conformity shall be as prescribed in Annex C.

IS 4584 : 2002 ANNEX B (Clause 5.1.2.3)
DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT OF TIMBER USED IN BRUSHES, SHOE POLISHING B-1 TEST SPECIMEN The entire block used in the brushes, shoe polishing may form the test specimen for determination of moisture content or a coupon cut from the test specimen may as well, be used for moisture content determination. When for any reason additional determination of moisture content is required, separate samples shall be prepared from the same material as is used in preparing the test specimens. Smaller specimens may be used when deemed necessary. The test shall be carried out immediately after cutting the specimen. B-2 APPARATUS B-2.1 Air Oven--Suitable to control the temperature of 105 � 2�C. B-2.2 Weighing Balance B-3 PROCEDURE Weigh accurately each test specimen. This specimen shall then be dried in a ventilated oven at a temperature of 105 � 2�C until the mass becomes constant between two successive weighing made at an interval of not less than 1 h. B-4 CALCULATION The moisture content, expressed as a percent of the dry mass is given by the formula: Moisture content = where W1 = initial mass in g of the test specimen, and W0 = dry mass in g of the test specimen.

ANNEX C (Clause 7)
SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY OF BRUSHES HAIR C-1 GENERAL Samples of brushes for testing shall be selected at random in the manner indicated below. C-2 METHOD OF SAMPLING C-2.1 Lot In any consignment, all the brushes of the same size and quality shall be divided into groups of 1 000 brushes or less and each such group shall constitute a lot. Care shall be taken to ensure that brushes included in a lot do not differ in construction as far as possible. C-2.1.1 The conformity of the brushes in a lot to the requirements of this standard shall be ascertained for each lot separately. The number of brushes to be selected for this purpose shall be in accordance with col 2 and 3 of Table 1.

Table 1 Scale of Sampling and Permissible Number of Defectives (Clauses C-2.1.1, C-2.1.2, C-3.1.1 and C-3.2)
Sl No. No. of Brushes in the Lot (2) Up to 50 51 to 100 101 to 200 201 to 300 301 to 500 501 and above No. of Brushes to be Selected in the Sample (3) 5 10 15 20 30 40 Permissible No. of Defective Brushes in the Sample (4) 0 1 1 2 3 3 No. of Brushes in the Sub-Sample (5) 4 4 8 8 12 16

i) ii) iii) iv) v) vi)

6

IS 4584 : 2002 C-2.1.2 The brushes shall be selected at random. To ensure randomness of selection one of the following procedures is recommended for use: a) If the brushes in a lot are packed in one box, then starting from any brush, count them in any suitable order as 1, 2, 3,....up to r which is the integral part of N/n (N and n being the lot size and sample size respectively). Every rth brush, thus counted shall be drawn to constitute the sample. b) If the brushes in a lot are packed in more than one box, approximately equal number of brushes shall be picked up at random from as many boxes as possible so as to obtain the required number of brushes as specified in Table 1. C-3 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY C-3.1 All the brushes selected according to C-2.1.1 and C-2.1.2 shall be examined for requirements given in 5.1 to 5.3, 5.7 and 5.8. Any brush not conforming to any one or more these requirements shall be considered as a defective. C-3.1.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements, if the number of defective brushes is less than or equal to the number given in col 4 of Table 1. C-3.2 In case the lot shall been found satisfactory in C-3.1.1, a sub-sample of size given in col 5 of Table 1 shall be taken at random from the sampled brushes. C-3.3 One-half of the brushes included in the subsample shall be taken and subjected to pull test or knock back test as the case may be (see 5.5). C-3.3.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this test, if none of the brushes tested fails the test. C-3.4 The other half of the brushes included in the sub-sample shall be taken and the weight of the filling material determined (see 5.4). C-3.4.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this test, if the weight of the filling material for each of the brushes lies within the specified tolerance.
